content.value_statement: Teams need reliable patterns for building LLM applications without unclear agent, memory, and retrieval choices. This skill provides structured LangChain architecture guidance for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains core LangChain concepts including agents, chains, memory, document processing, and callbacks.
Provides example architecture patterns for RAG, custom agents, multi-step chains, and memory selection.
Outlines testing approaches for agent tool selection and memory persistence.
Covers performance practices such as caching, batch processing, and streaming responses.
Includes a production checklist for error handling, logging, rate limits, validation, and observability.
limitations: The package contains only SKILL.md, so referenced resource and asset files are not included.
Some examples use older LangChain import paths that may need updates for current versions.
The skill provides architecture guidance, not a complete production application.
Security controls for real tools, email sending, and external APIs must be designed separately.

use_cases.title: Plan a RAG Application
use_cases.description: Select document loaders, splitters, vector stores, retrievers, and source-return settings for a retrieval workflow.

use_cases.title: Design an Agent Workflow
use_cases.description: Choose agent types, tool descriptions, memory behavior, callbacks, and safeguards for a multi-step LLM assistant.

use_cases.title: Review Production Readiness
use_cases.description: Check error handling, observability, rate limits, validation, fallback behavior, and token-cost monitoring before release.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a LangChain Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose a LangChain architecture for my application. My goal is [goal], my data source is [source], and users need [workflow].

prompt_templates.title: Design a RAG Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a LangChain RAG pipeline for [documents]. Include loading, splitting, embeddings, vector storage, retrieval settings, and source handling.

prompt_templates.title: Architect an Agent System
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a LangChain agent workflow with tools for [tasks]. Include tool descriptions, memory choice, callback monitoring, failure handling, and test cases.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this LangChain design for production readiness: [design]. Identify risks, missing controls, performance issues, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: I need a RAG assistant for internal policy documents.
output_examples.output: Recommended design: load policy documents, split them into overlapping chunks, store embeddings in a vector store, retrieve top matches, and return source references with each answer.

output_examples.input: I want an agent that can search internal data and send follow-up messages.
output_examples.output: Suggested review: define each tool narrowly, require confirmation before sending messages, add callback logging, limit execution time, and test tool selection with mocked model responses.

output_examples.input: Our LangChain prototype is slow and hard to debug.
output_examples.output: Focus areas: add callbacks for latency and token tracking, enable caching for repeated prompts, batch document processing, and create failure tests for agent and memory behavior.

best_practices: Start with the simplest chain or retrieval pattern that satisfies the workflow.
Add callbacks early so latency, token usage, tool calls, and failures are visible.
Validate inputs and tool permissions before allowing agents to act on external systems.
anti_patterns: Do not give agents broad tools without clear descriptions, limits, and confirmation rules.
Do not store unlimited conversation history without windowing or summarization.
Do not ship retrieval systems without checking chunk quality, source coverage, and answer grounding.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps plan LangChain applications that use agents, chains, memory, retrieval, callbacks, and production safeguards.

faq.question: Does it generate a complete application?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture guidance and examples that you adapt to your codebase and LangChain version.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it include security guidance?
faq.answer: It includes a production checklist with validation, rate limiting, timeouts, logging, and observability items.

faq.question: Are all referenced files included?
faq.answer: No. The package only contains SKILL.md, so referenced resources and assets are not available in this package.

faq.question: What should I check before implementation?
faq.answer: Confirm current LangChain APIs, define tool permissions, choose memory limits, and add tests for tool selection and failure handling.
